§6.2: приложенная сила, не превышающая μ_s·N, уравновешивается трением покоя, и система остаётся в покое
§6.3: the centripetal force is the mass times the centripetal acceleration computed in §4.4
§6.3: центростремительная сила есть масса, умноженная на центростремительное ускорение, вычисленное в §4.4
§6.2: a contact between two surfaces, to which the coefficients of friction belong
§6.2: контакт двух поверхностей, которому принадлежат коэффициенты трения
§6.2: the magnitude of kinetic friction is f_k = μ_k·N
§6.2: модуль трения скольжения равен f_k = μ_k·N

texts.text:
<definition id="fs-id1165039114071">
<term>Newton’s first law of motion</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1165039091047">body at rest remains at rest or, if in motion, remains in motion at constant velocity unless acted on by a net external force; also known as the law of inertia</meaning>
</definition>

<definition id="fs-id1165039302065">
<term>inertia</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1165039091658">ability of an object to resist changes in its motion</meaning>
</definition>

<definition id="fs-id1165039108359">
<term>inertial reference frame</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1165039210665">reference frame moving at constant velocity relative to an inertial frame is also inertial; a reference frame accelerating relative to an inertial frame is not inertial</meaning>
</definition>

<definition id="fs-id1165039477315">
<term>Newton’s second law of motion</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1165039477320">acceleration of a system is directly proportional to and in the same direction as the net external force acting on the system and is inversely proportional to its mass</meaning>
</definition>

<note id="fs-id1165039096883">
<title>Newton’s Second Law of Motion</title>
<para id="fs-id1165038999240">The acceleration of a system is directly proportional to and in the same direction as the net external force acting on the system and is inversely proportional to its mass. In equation form, Newton’s second law is</para>
<equation id="fs-id1165039299982" class="unnumbered"><label/><m:math><m:mrow><m:mstyle mathvariant="bold" mathsize="normal"><m:mover accent="true"><m:mi>a</m:mi><m:mo stretchy="false">→</m:mo></m:mover></m:mstyle><m:mo>=</m:mo><m:mfrac><m:mrow><m:msub><m:mstyle mathvariant="bold" mathsize="normal"><m:mover accent="true"><m:mi>F</m:mi><m:mo stretchy="false">→</m:mo></m:mover></m:mstyle><m:mrow><m:mtext>net</m:mtext></m:mrow></m:msub></m:mrow><m:mi>m</m:mi></m:mfrac><m:mo>,</m:mo></m:mrow></m:math></equation>
<para id="fs-id1165039257622">where <m:math><m:mstyle mathvariant="bold" mathsize="normal"><m:mover accent="true"><m:mi>a</m:mi><m:mo stretchy="false">→</m:mo></m:mover></m:mstyle></m:math> is the acceleration, <m:math><m:mrow><m:msub><m:mstyle mathvariant="bold" mathsize="normal"><m:mover accent="true"><m:mi>F</m:mi><m:mo stretchy="false">→</m:mo></m:mover></m:mstyle><m:mrow><m:mtext>net</m:mtext></m:mrow></m:msub></m:mrow></m:math> is the net force, and <emphasis effect="italics">m</emphasis> is the mass. This is often written in the more familiar form</para>
<equation id="fs-id1165039079819"><m:math><m:mrow><m:msub><m:mstyle mathvariant="bold" mathsize="normal"><m:mover accent="true"><m:mi>F</m:mi><m:mo stretchy="false">→</m:mo></m:mover></m:mstyle><m:mrow><m:mtext>net</m:mtext></m:mrow></m:msub><m:mo>=</m:mo><m:mstyle displaystyle="true"><m:mo>∑</m:mo><m:mrow><m:mstyle mathvariant="bold" mathsize="normal"><m:mover accent="true"><m:mi>F</m:mi><m:mo stretchy="false">→</m:mo></m:mover></m:mstyle><m:mo>=</m:mo><m:mi>m</m:mi><m:mstyle mathvariant="bold" mathsize="normal"><m:mover accent="true"><m:mi>a</m:mi><m:mo stretchy="false">→</m:mo></m:mover></m:mstyle></m:mrow></m:mstyle><m:mo>,</m:mo></m:mrow></m:math></equation>
<para id="fs-id1165039083076">but the first equation gives more insight into what Newton’s second law means. When only the magnitude of force and acceleration are considered, this equation can be written in the simpler scalar form:</para>
<equation id="fs-id1165039009387"><m:math><m:mrow><m:msub><m:mi>F</m:mi><m:mrow><m:mtext>net</m:mtext></m:mrow></m:msub><m:mo>=</m:mo><m:mi>m</m:mi><m:mi>a</m:mi><m:mo>.</m:mo></m:mrow></m:math></equation>
</note>

<definition id="fs-id1165036785178">
<term>weight</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1165036785184">force <m:math><m:mstyle mathvariant="bold" mathsize="normal"><m:mover accent="true"><m:mi>w</m:mi><m:mo stretchy="false">→</m:mo></m:mover></m:mstyle></m:math> due to gravity acting on an object of mass <emphasis effect="italics">m</emphasis></meaning>
</definition>

<definition id="fs-id1165036735376">
<term>Newton’s third law of motion</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1165036735382">whenever one body exerts a force on a second body, the first body experiences a force that is equal in magnitude and opposite in direction to the force that it exerts</meaning>
</definition>

<definition id="fs-id1165038031500">
<term>friction</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1165037166731">force that opposes relative motion or attempts at motion between systems in contact</meaning>
</definition>

<definition id="fs-id1165038337854">
<term>kinetic friction</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1165036846768">force that opposes the motion of two systems that are in contact and moving relative to each other</meaning>
</definition>

<note id="fs-id1165038277974">
<title>Magnitude of Kinetic Friction</title>
<para id="fs-id1165037149957">The magnitude of kinetic friction <m:math><m:mrow><m:msub><m:mi>f</m:mi><m:mtext>k</m:mtext></m:msub></m:mrow></m:math> is given by</para>
<equation id="fs-id1165038157609"><m:math><m:mrow><m:msub><m:mi>f</m:mi><m:mtext>k</m:mtext></m:msub><m:mo>=</m:mo><m:msub><m:mi>μ</m:mi><m:mtext>k</m:mtext></m:msub><m:mi>N</m:mi><m:mo>,</m:mo></m:mrow></m:math></equation>
<para id="fs-id1165038293964">where <m:math><m:mrow><m:msub><m:mi>μ</m:mi><m:mtext>k</m:mtext></m:msub></m:mrow></m:math> is the <term class="no-emphasis" id="term-00005">coefficient of kinetic friction</term>.</para>
</note>

<definition id="fs-id1165036846773">
<term>static friction</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1165038327277">force that opposes the motion of two systems that are in contact and are not moving relative to each other</meaning>
</definition>

<note id="fs-id1165036855503">
<title>Magnitude of Static Friction</title>
<para id="fs-id1165037982016">The magnitude of static friction <m:math><m:mrow><m:msub><m:mi>f</m:mi><m:mtext>s</m:mtext></m:msub></m:mrow></m:math> is</para>
<equation id="fs-id1165037176402"><m:math><m:mrow><m:msub><m:mi>f</m:mi><m:mtext>s</m:mtext></m:msub><m:mo>≤</m:mo><m:msub><m:mi>μ</m:mi><m:mtext>s</m:mtext></m:msub><m:mi>N</m:mi><m:mo>,</m:mo></m:mrow></m:math></equation>
<para id="fs-id1165038241878">where <m:math><m:mrow><m:msub><m:mi>μ</m:mi><m:mtext>s</m:mtext></m:msub></m:mrow></m:math> is the <term class="no-emphasis" id="term-00004">coefficient of static friction</term> and <emphasis effect="italics">N</emphasis> is the magnitude of the normal force.</para>
</note>

<definition id="fs-id1165039353624">
<term>centripetal force</term>
<meaning id="fs-id1165039106544">any net force causing uniform circular motion</meaning>
</definition>

labels.text: §5.4: w = mg — weight is the mass multiplied by the acceleration due to gravity
§5.4: w = mg — вес есть масса, умноженная на ускорение свободного падения
§5.2: a body at rest remains at rest, and a body in motion remains in motion at constant velocity, unless acted upon by a net external force
§5.2: покоящееся тело остаётся в покое, а движущееся сохраняет постоянную скорость, пока на него не подействует результирующая внешняя сила
§6.2: the force applied parallel to the surfaces, which friction opposes
§6.2: сила, приложенная вдоль поверхностей, которой противодействует трение
§6.3: F_c = m·a_c — the net force directed toward the centre that keeps the body on its circular path
§6.3: F_c = m·a_c — направленная к центру результирующая сила, удерживающая тело на круговой траектории
§5.2 read through Lex. I: the body is compelled to change its state by impressed forces
§5.2 в прочтении Lex. I: тело вынуждено изменить своё состояние приложенными силами
§6.2: the system rests on or slides along the presented contact of surfaces
§6.2: система покоится на предъявленном контакте поверхностей или скользит по нему
§5.5: the case presents the force the first system exerts on the second
§5.5: дело предъявляет силу, с которой первая система действует на вторую
§5.4: the acceleration due to gravity at the place of the system
§5.4: ускорение свободного падения в месте нахождения системы
the case states that the system and the Principia body are one and the same
дело сообщает, что система и тело Principia — одно и то же
§5.2: the case states the system is observed from an inertial reference frame
§5.2: дело сообщает, что система наблюдается из инерциальной системы отсчёта
§6.2: μ_k, the coefficient of kinetic friction of this pair of surfaces
§6.2: μ_k — коэффициент трения скольжения этой пары поверхностей
§6.2: f_k = μ_k·N — the magnitude of kinetic friction, which does not depend on the applied force
§6.2: f_k = μ_k·N — модуль трения скольжения, не зависящий от приложенной силы
§5.3: the mass of the system — the quantity of matter, a measure of its inertia
§5.3: масса системы — количество вещества, мера её инертности
§6.2: μ_s·N — the greatest force static friction can supply before the surfaces begin to slide
§6.2: μ_s·N — наибольшая сила, которую способно дать трение покоя, прежде чем поверхности начнут скользить
the case states the system moves as the presented kinematic body
дело сообщает, что система движется как предъявленное кинематическое тело
§5.3: the net external force on the system — the vector sum of all external forces
§5.3: результирующая внешняя сила на систему — векторная сумма всех внешних сил
§6.2: the normal force N pressing the two surfaces together
§6.2: сила нормального давления N, прижимающая поверхности друг к другу
§5.5: whenever one body exerts a force on a second, the second exerts a force equal in magnitude and opposite in direction on the first
§5.5: если одно тело действует на другое с некоторой силой, второе действует на первое с силой, равной по модулю и противоположной по направлению
§5.2: Newton's first law — the system remains at rest or in uniform motion in a straight line
§5.2: первый закон Ньютона — система сохраняет покой или равномерное прямолинейное движение
§6.2: μ_s, the coefficient of static friction of this pair of surfaces — dimensionless, since it is a ratio of two forces
§6.2: μ_s — коэффициент трения покоя этой пары поверхностей; безразмерен, ибо есть отношение двух сил
§6.2: static friction is able to balance the applied force, and the system does not slide
§6.2: трение покоя уравновешивает приложенную силу, и система не скользит
§5.4: w = mg — the weight of the system, the force of gravity on it
§5.4: w = mg — вес системы, сила тяжести, действующая на неё
